headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if pdf.js output is fed into a prompt-leak workflow; otherwise direct data leakage and capability conflict are limited by no network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: pdf.js ingests PDF files and can run in browser-based tests, while system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage. No shared channel is documented, so the pairwise injection path is inferred rather than proven. If pdf.js output is copied into the other agent’s prompt or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled PDF text could steer downstream behavior.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into system_prompts_leaks prompts or a shared workspace exists
IF PDF content is treated as instruction-bearing text by the downstream agent
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Strip PDF text to plain data before reuse
Disable copy-paste of raw extracted text into prompts
Add a provenance banner to extracted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress, while system_prompts_leaks also has no network egress and no data classes touched are listed. With no shared filesystem or OAuth scopes documented, direct leakage is not evidenced; the remaining risk is limited to manual transfer of PDF contents into the other agent.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same PDF workspace
IF sensitive PDF contents are manually copied from pdf.js into system_prompts_leaks
mitigations: Review logs for accidental content duplication

C_capability_conflict.rationale: pdf.js supports multiple instances and writes only PDF files; system_prompts_leaks exposes no write surfaces or mutable-resource scopes. No overlapping write target is documented, so a real conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not show shared filesystem, git, or OAuth mutation paths.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable resource
mitigations: Run one agent at a time for shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted PDF text, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak oriented agent that may treat upstream text as meaningful input. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default document-processing workflows if A’s output is forwarded to B without verification. Because no explicit validation boundary is documented, uncertainty should be resolved upward.
conditions: IF pdf.js extraction output is forwarded into system_prompts_leaks without a verification step
IF downstream actions rely on the extracted text as authoritative
mitigations: Require schema validation on extracted text
Limit downstream actions to read-only review
requires-engineering: add automated verification before reuse

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented. pdf.js only lists PDF documents and system_prompts_leaks lists no data classes or compliance constraints, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF future profiles add regulated data classes or residency constraints
IF either agent is deployed under a policy requiring documented retention controls
